_readme: The subject of the benchmark. `scripts/evaluate.py --model` defaults to `current.hf_model`,
so 'evaluate the model' has one unambiguous answer and a comparison always names what it
This file is DATA, not a claim of quality in the abstract. `reason` states what the
designation rests on, `evidence` says where to check it, and `qualification` states what
the designation does NOT mean. Change it in a deliberate commit that cites new evidence --
never as a side effect of a run, and never by a script. Nothing in this repo writes it.
`hf_model` is `artifacts/hf-tt-tnt-1024` -- ONE fixed directory that gets overwritten with
whatever the current best idea for this size is, rather than a new suffixed sibling per
experiment. See CLAUDE.md's 2026-08-29 consolidation entry. The raw training checkpoints
under artifacts/checkpoints-* are untouched by that convention -- only the derived,
cheaply-regeneratable HF conversions are collapsed to one.
UPDATED 2026-09-24: promoted from the 2026-08-29 dialogue checkpoint to a Stage A + Stage B
checkpoint (data-scale-up spec). Stage A alone (pure FineWeb-Edu pretraining to the full
Chinchilla-matched budget) confirmed-significantly REGRESSED narrative coherence -- Stage B
(a curated-blend continued-training pass on top) confirmed-significantly fixed that
regression while keeping nearly all of Stage A's loss/commonsense gains. See `qualification`
for exactly what is and is not established.

current.label: tt-tnt-1024
current.reason: Stage A + Stage B (data-scale-up spec, docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-01-data-scale-up-design.md): Stage A continued the 2026-08-29 dialogue checkpoint on 2,529,270,500 tokens of pure FineWeb-Edu (7.2x the prior training-token count, reaching the spec's 2.46B Chinchilla-matched target for 123M params), then Stage B continued that for one more epoch (10,761 steps) on the curated ten-source blend (`tokens-v4`, the same corpus the checkpoint being replaced trained on). External-benchmark gains carried through both stages: wikitext bits/byte 1.4584 -> 1.2551 (-0.2033), lambada_openai accuracy 0.0980 -> 0.2135, piqa 0.5484 -> 0.5925, arc_easy 0.3106 -> 0.4272, arc_challenge 0.1783 -> 0.2133 -- all measured via the same scripts/benchmark_external.py suite, same 512-token window, same lm-eval 0.4.9, docs/measurements/external-tt-tnt-1024-stageb.md. MMLU stayed flat throughout (0.2295 -> 0.2292), which is expected and separately confirmed (see qualification), not a regression. StoryCloze (scripts/eval_storycloze.py, forced-choice narrative continuation, the instrument this project substituted for the literal StoryBench paper) is the reason Stage B exists: Stage A alone significantly REGRESSED narrative coherence versus the prior designated checkpoint (0.6062 -> 0.5725, paired sign test p=0.00504, docs/measurements/storycloze-tt-tnt-1024-vs-stagea-full.json), and Stage B significantly reversed that regression versus Stage A (0.5725 -> 0.6161, paired sign test p=6.2e-05, docs/measurements/storycloze-stagea-full-vs-stageb.json) while landing statistically indistinguishable from the prior checkpoint (p=0.326, not a confirmed beat -- see qualification). Q&A capability spot-checked and intact: greedy 'Q: What is the capital of France?\nAnswer:' -> 'The capital of France is Paris.' (correct, before the model's known repetition-loop tail).
current.qualification: Three things this designation does NOT establish. (1) StoryCloze recovery is a fix of a regression, not a confirmed improvement over the checkpoint being replaced: the paired comparison against the prior designated checkpoint is NOT significant (p=0.326, 109 vs 94 discordant pairs of 1511) -- the honest claim is 'no longer significantly worse', not 'better'. Read the raw accuracy numbers (0.6161 vs 0.6062) as a point estimate, not a proven gain. (2) MMLU/ARC-Challenge staying flat across a 7.2x increase in pretraining tokens (confirmed across three points: 0.2295 / 0.2297 / 0.2292) means this checkpoint has NOT gained general factual knowledge -- it is measurably more fluent and better at commonsense/narrative tasks, not smarter in the MMLU sense, and the model card must not blur that distinction. (3) Stage A's corpus composition and token count moved together (100% FineWeb-Edu web text replacing a fraction of the curated blend's share, not an isolated token-count ablation), so 'more tokens helped' and 'the corpus shifted toward web-educational register' are confounded in the external-benchmark gains, even though Stage B's own comparison against Stage A is a clean single-corpus continuation. Separately, unchanged from the prior designation: this is still a 512-token-window model (evaluate() and scripts/benchmark_external.py both windowed at 512 for every comparison above, so all these numbers are mutually comparable but not comparable to tt-tnt-v3's 2048-window figures), and the growing-conversation KV-cache crash mitigation (chat template capping rendered history at 5 messages) is unchanged and still required at serve time.

corpus.tokens_dir: artifacts/tokens-v4 (Stage B only -- Stage A trained on artifacts/tokens-stagea + artifacts/tokens-stagea-inc, pure FineWeb-Edu, not part of the registered SOURCES blend)
corpus.note: Stage B's curated-blend digest and token count are unchanged from the prior designation (same tokens-v4 corpus, same ten sources) -- what changed is that these weights ALSO trained on 2,529,270,500 tokens of pure FineWeb-Edu (Stage A) before Stage B ran. That FineWeb-Edu training does not go through train/corpus.py's SOURCES registry or blend_corpus.py at all -- it was fetched and tokenized as a standalone corpus (artifacts/tokens-stagea, artifacts/tokens-stagea-inc), so it has no target_share/upsample/blend_sha256 of its own to record here. docs/corpus_blend.md still describes only the curated-blend side of this checkpoint's training; the FineWeb-Edu side is documented in CLAUDE.md's 2026-09-22/23 and 2026-09-24 entries instead.
